text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.87% today to $142.13, continuing a sharp two-week rally of 13.6%. The move reflects escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—container ships are being attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Aramco facilities have come under strike, triggering genuine concern about oil supply disruptions. This pushed global oil prices to $125.44 per barrel today, while U.S. crude climbed to $96.24, and oil companies like ConocoPhillips benefit directly when crude prices rise because they sell at these higher rates.

The broader context: the International Energy Agency has now warned publicly that diesel supply will stay squeezed through 2027 due to Iran-related disruption, falling inventories, and steady demand. That kind of structural supply tightness—not just a temporary price spike—tends to support energy stocks over time, which likely explains why the stock has gained more than 13% in just two weeks as the conflict risks have become clearer.
